q: A purchase order is placed on a supplier for stores valued at Rs 7,50,000. The security deposit prescribed under the contract at 5 per cent of the order value works out to:
e: Security Deposit = 5% of the order value = 0.05 x Rs 7,50,000 = Rs 37,500.

q: Nine wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 3 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 700 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Demurrage = wagons x days detained beyond free time x rate = 9 x 3 x Rs 700 = Rs 18,900.

q: The minimum level of an item is 620 units and the maximum level is 2,260 units. The average stock level of the item is:

options.A: 1,440 units
options.B: 1,380 units
options.C: 1,500 units
options.D: 1,640 units

e: Average stock level = (minimum level + maximum level) / 2 = (620 + 2,260) / 2 = 1,440 units.

q: A depot holds 3,400 units of an item, whereas the maximum level fixed for the item is 2,900 units. The book rate of the item is Rs 36 per unit. The value of the stock held in excess of the maximum level is:
e: Stock held above the maximum level = 3,400 - 2,900 = 500 units; value of the excess stock = 500 x Rs 36 = Rs 18,000.

q: The average consumption of an item is 60 units per day and the lead time for emergency procurement is 6 days. The danger level of the item is:

options.A: 300 units
options.B: 330 units
options.C: 360 units
options.D: 420 units

e: Danger level = average daily consumption x lead time for emergency procurement = 60 x 6 = 360 units.

q: In carrying out an ABC analysis of stores items, the items are first arranged in:

options.A: Ascending order of their annual consumption value
options.B: Descending order of their annual consumption value
options.C: Alphabetical order of their PL numbers
options.D: Descending order of their unit price

e: In ABC analysis, the items are first arranged in descending order of their annual consumption value; the few high-value items then form category A, followed by categories B and C.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 7,200 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 80 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 5 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:

options.A: 400 units
options.B: 600 units
options.C: 480 units
options.D: 960 units

q: 'Cycle stock' of a stores item means:

options.A: The stock held in excess of the maximum level fixed for the item
options.B: The stock reserved only for meeting emergencies
options.C: The stock awaiting inspection and acceptance at the depot
options.D: The stock which is regularly consumed and replenished between two successive receipts of the item

e: Cycle stock is the stock which is regularly consumed and replenished between two successive receipts of the item; it rises when a fresh lot is received and runs down with issues until the next receipt.

q: A depot holds 750 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 24 per unit. A fresh receipt of 250 units is taken into stock at Rs 44 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:

options.A: Rs 24 per unit
options.B: Rs 34 per unit
options.C: Rs 44 per unit
options.D: Rs 29 per unit

e: Revised book (average) rate = (750 x Rs 24 + 250 x Rs 44) / 1,000 = Rs 29,000 / 1,000 = Rs 29 per unit.

q: The Stores Miscellaneous Suspense head differs from the Purchase Suspense head in that the Stores Miscellaneous Suspense accommodates:

options.A: Bills paid for stores of which the material has not yet been received
options.B: The value of stores issued, e.g. to other railways, departments or firms, pending final adjustment or recovery
options.C: The money deposited by purchasers of scrap, pending delivery of the material to them
options.D: Differences of quantity and value found in stock verification

e: Stores Miscellaneous Suspense accommodates the value of stores issued, e.g. to other railways, departments or firms, pending final adjustment or recovery; Purchase Suspense, in contrast, covers bills paid for stores not yet received and linked.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 57 lakh and the total issues during the year are Rs 3 crore. The Turnover Ratio of stores is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance of stores / total issues = Rs 57 lakh / Rs 3 crore = 0.19.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The buffer (safety) stock of an item forms a part of its normal cycle stock and is consumed in every replenishment cycle.
2. The buffer (safety) stock is drawn upon only when the consumption exceeds the normal rate or the replenishment of stock is delayed.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is wrong - the buffer stock is not a part of the normal cycle stock and is not consumed in every cycle. Statement 2 is correct - it is drawn upon only when consumption exceeds the normal rate or replenishment is delayed.

q: The AAC of an item is 7,200 units. The stock in hand is 1,050 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 450 units. The coverage available for the item is:

options.A: 1.75 months
options.B: 0.75 month
options.C: 2.5 months
options.D: 3 months

e: Coverage = (stock in hand + dues) / AAC x 12 = (1,050 + 450) / 7,200 x 12 = 2.5 months.

q: Receipts and issues of a stores item are recorded in the Priced Stores Ledger in:

options.A: The unit in which the supplier has billed for the item
options.B: Metric tonnes in all cases
options.C: The unit decided by the depot storekeeper for each transaction
options.D: The unit of account (e.g. number, kilogram or litre) prescribed for the item in the Priced Vocabulary

e: Receipts and issues in the Priced Stores Ledger are recorded in the unit of account prescribed for the item in the Priced Vocabulary, e.g. number, kilogram or litre, ensuring uniform accounting of the item.

q: The average consumption of an item is 175 units per week, the lead time for its procurement is 5 weeks and the safety (buffer) stock provided for it is 375 units. The re-order level of the item is:

options.A: 875 units
options.B: 1,250 units
options.C: 1,400 units
options.D: 500 units

e: Re-order level = (average consumption x lead time) + safety stock = (175 x 5) + 375 = 875 + 375 = 1,250 units.

q: An 'indent' in stores procedure is distinguished from a 'purchase order' in that an indent is:

options.A: An internal demand placed for the procurement of stores, whereas a purchase order is the order placed on a supplier for their supply
options.B: An order placed on a supplier, whereas a purchase order is an internal demand for stores
options.C: A demand for stores required immediately, whereas a purchase order is for stores required in future
options.D: A document issued by the Accounts Department, whereas a purchase order is issued by the supplier

e: An indent is an internal demand raised within the Railways for the procurement of stores, whereas a purchase order is the order placed on a supplier for their supply; the indent precedes the purchase order.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,650 units. The average consumption is 140 units per week and the average lead time is 8 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:

options.A: 650 units
options.B: 420 units
options.C: 530 units
options.D: 1,650 units

e: Minimum stock level = re-order level - (average consumption x average lead time) = 1,650 - (140 x 8) = 1,650 - 1,120 = 530 units.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The re-order level, minimum level and maximum level of a stock item are fixed with reference to its AAC, lead time and pattern of consumption.
2. Once fixed, the stock levels of an item are never revised, even if its consumption pattern changes materially.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct - the re-order, minimum and maximum levels are fixed with reference to the item's AAC, lead time and pattern of consumption. Statement 2 is wrong - the levels are revised when the consumption pattern changes materially.

q: The re-order level of an item is 2,050 units and the re-order quantity is 1,300 units. The minimum consumption is 75 units per week and the minimum lead time is 6 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:

options.A: 3,350 units
options.B: 2,800 units
options.C: 2,600 units
options.D: 2,900 units

e: Maximum stock level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 2,050 + 1,300 - (75 x 6) = 2,900 units.

q: The departmental charges levied in addition to the book value on stores issued to outside parties represent, broadly:

options.A: A profit margin earned by the Railways on the issue of the stores
options.B: The freight payable for despatch of the stores to the party
options.C: The cost incurred by the Railways on handling, storage, supervision and accounting of the stores
options.D: The customs duty paid by the Railways on the stores

e: Departmental charges levied on stores issued to outside parties represent the cost incurred by the Railways on handling, storage, supervision and accounting of the stores; they are a recovery of cost, not a profit margin.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 275 units per week, its normal consumption is 215 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 7 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided for the item is:

options.A: 350 units
options.B: 420 units
options.C: 490 units
options.D: 60 units

e: Safety stock = (maximum consumption - normal consumption) x lead time = (275 - 215) x 7 = 420 units.

q: The Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) of a stores item is also known as its:

options.A: Economic lot size
options.B: Average order size
options.C: Minimum lot size
options.D: Standard purchase quantity

e: The Economic Order Quantity is also known as the economic lot size - the order quantity at which the total of the annual ordering cost and carrying cost is the minimum.

q: The average consumption of an item is 240 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 9 weeks. The consumption of the item during the lead time is:

options.A: 1,920 units
options.B: 2,400 units
options.C: 216 units
options.D: 2,160 units

e: Lead time consumption = average consumption per week x lead time in weeks = 240 x 9 = 2,160 units.

q: In ABC analysis, 'B' category items are subjected to:

options.A: The same close control as 'A' category items
options.B: No control at all, as they are insignificant in value
options.C: Moderate control - less close than that exercised over 'A' category items but closer than that over 'C' category items
options.D: Control only at the time of the annual stock verification

e: In ABC analysis, B category items are of moderate value and are subjected to moderate control - less close than the control over A category items but closer than that over C category items.

q: The average consumption of an item is 75 units per day and the lead time for emergency procurement is 8 days. The danger level of the item is:

options.A: 600 units
options.B: 450 units
options.C: 525 units
options.D: 750 units

e: Danger level = average daily consumption x lead time for emergency procurement = 75 x 8 = 600 units.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where a stores tender cannot be decided within the validity period of the offers, the tenderers may be requested to extend the validity of their offers.
2. A tenderer who does not agree to extend the validity of his offer is entitled to the refund of his earnest money.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct - where a tender cannot be decided within the validity period of the offers, tenderers may be requested to extend the validity, and a tenderer who does not agree to extend is entitled to refund of his earnest money.

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 26 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 475 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:
e: Value of the shortage = units short x book rate = 26 x Rs 475 = Rs 12,350, to be accounted for through the Stock Adjustment Account pending investigation and write-off.

q: The inventory carrying cost of stores is also known as the:

options.A: Ordering cost
options.B: Stock-out cost
options.C: Procurement cost
options.D: Holding cost

e: The inventory carrying cost of stores is also known as the holding cost - the cost of holding stock, comprising interest on the capital locked up, storage, insurance and obsolescence.

q: During stock verification, 32 units of an item are found in excess of the book balance. The book rate of the item is Rs 85 per unit. The value of the excess taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account is:
e: Value of the excess = units found excess x book rate = 32 x Rs 85 = Rs 2,720, taken into stock with credit to the Stock Adjustment Account.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Stores items which have become non-moving in a depot are straightaway condemned and sold as scrap.
2. Non-moving items are first reviewed, and serviceable items usable elsewhere are transferred or declared surplus; only items which are unserviceable are condemned and disposed of as scrap.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is wrong - non-moving items are not straightaway condemned and scrapped. Statement 2 is correct - they are first reviewed; serviceable items usable elsewhere are transferred or declared surplus, and only unserviceable items are condemned and disposed of as scrap.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 5,50,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 3 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay amount to:
e: Liquidated damages = 0.5% of the value of stores in arrear for each week of delay = 0.005 x Rs 5,50,000 x 3 = Rs 8,250.

q: A purchase order placed on a supplier for stores ordinarily specifies:

options.A: Only the total value of the order
options.B: The description and PL number of the stores, the quantity and rate, the consignee depot and the delivery period
options.C: Only the name of the supplier and the description of the item
options.D: The names of the other tenderers who had quoted for the item

e: A purchase order ordinarily specifies the description and PL number of the stores, the quantity and rate, the consignee depot and the delivery period, which together form the complete terms of the supply.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 6,25,000. The advance payment admissible at 98 per cent of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
e: Advance payment = 98% of the bill value = 0.98 x Rs 6,25,000 = Rs 6,12,500, paid against the inspection certificate and despatch documents.

q: While covering a demand for a stock item, the quantity to be ordered is worked out after taking into account the stock in hand and the dues, mainly in order to:

options.A: Avoid duplicate ordering of quantities which are already on order
options.B: Reduce the AAC fixed for the item
options.C: Increase the coverage period of the item
options.D: Fix the book rate of the item

e: While covering a demand, the stock in hand and the dues (quantities already on order) are taken into account mainly to avoid duplicate ordering of quantities which are already on order.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 48 lakh, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 1.92 crore and issues during the year are Rs 1.78 crore. The closing balance of stores is:

options.A: Rs 58 lakh
options.B: Rs 66 lakh
options.C: Rs 62 lakh
options.D: Rs 74 lakh

e: Closing balance of stores = opening balance + receipts - issues = Rs 48 lakh + Rs 1.92 crore - Rs 1.78 crore = Rs 62 lakh.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 72 lakh and its Turnover Ratio is 0.24. The total issues of stores during the year are:

options.A: Rs 2.88 crore
options.B: Rs 3 crore
options.C: Rs 3.6 crore
options.D: Rs 30 crore

e: Total issues = closing balance / Turnover Ratio = Rs 72 lakh / 0.24 = Rs 3 crore.

q: The AAC of an item is 11,400 units. Coverage for four months is required to be provided. The stock in hand is 1,100 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 600 units. The quantity to be ordered is:

options.A: 2,700 units
options.B: 3,200 units
options.C: 3,800 units
options.D: 2,100 units

e: Quantity to order = requirement for 4 months - stock - dues = (11,400 x 4/12) - 1,100 - 600 = 3,800 - 1,700 = 2,100 units.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 1.45 crore and the closing balance is Rs 95 lakh. The average stock held during the year is:

options.A: Rs 1.20 crore
options.B: Rs 95 lakh
options.C: Rs 1.45 crore
options.D: Rs 2.40 crore

e: Average stock held = (opening balance + closing balance) / 2 = (Rs 1.45 crore + Rs 95 lakh) / 2 = Rs 1.20 crore.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 2.2 crore. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 16 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:

options.A: Rs 22 lakh
options.B: Rs 44 lakh
options.C: Rs 35.2 lakh
options.D: Rs 3.52 lakh

e: Annual inventory carrying cost = average stock value x carrying cost rate = Rs 2.2 crore x 16% = Rs 35.2 lakh.

q: The safety (buffer) stock of an item is 260 units and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 16 per unit per year. The annual carrying cost attributable to the safety stock is:
e: Annual carrying cost of the safety stock = safety stock x carrying cost per unit = 260 x Rs 16 = Rs 4,160.

q: A stores depot issues 940 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 38 per unit. The value of the issue debited to the consuming department is:
e: Issue value = quantity issued x book rate = 940 x Rs 38 = Rs 35,720, debited to the consuming department at the book (average) rate.

q: A supplier fails to supply 1,250 units of stores contracted at Rs 58 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 69 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost = quantity x (risk purchase rate - contract rate) = 1,250 x (Rs 69 - Rs 58) = 1,250 x Rs 11 = Rs 13,750, recoverable from the defaulting supplier.

q: Eight wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 6 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 900 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Demurrage = wagons x days detained beyond free time x rate = 8 x 6 x Rs 900 = Rs 43,200.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 22 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 74 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 63 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:

options.A: A debit balance of Rs 11 lakh
options.B: A debit balance of Rs 33 lakh
options.C: A credit balance of Rs 33 lakh
options.D: A debit balance of Rs 85 lakh

e: Closing Purchase Suspense = opening debit + bills paid - material received and linked = 22 + 74 - 63 = a debit balance of Rs 33 lakh.

q: A depot holds 2,750 units of an item. The book rate of the item is revised from Rs 110 to Rs 118 per unit. The change in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:

options.A: An increase of Rs 13,750
options.B: A decrease of Rs 22,000
options.C: An increase of Rs 27,500
options.D: An increase of Rs 22,000

e: Change in stock value = quantity in hand x rise in book rate = 2,750 x (Rs 118 - Rs 110) = 2,750 x Rs 8 = an increase of Rs 22,000, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: A purchase order is placed on a supplier for stores valued at Rs 9,00,000. The security deposit prescribed under the contract at 5 per cent of the order value works out to:
e: Security Deposit = 5% of the order value = 0.05 x Rs 9,00,000 = Rs 45,000.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 14,400 units and the quantity ordered each time (Economic Order Quantity) is 900 units. The number of orders to be placed during the year is:
e: Number of orders per year = annual requirement / EOQ = 14,400 / 900 = 16 orders.

q: A depot holds an opening stock of 1,900 units of an item. During the year, 1,150 units are received into stock and 2,050 units are issued. The book rate of the item is Rs 52 per unit. The value of the closing stock of the item is:
e: Closing stock quantity = 1,900 + 1,150 - 2,050 = 1,000 units; value of the closing stock = 1,000 x Rs 52 = Rs 52,000.

q: A stores depot issues 500 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 120 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable at 12.5 per cent of the book value. The total amount recoverable from the party is:
e: Total recoverable = book value + departmental charges = (500 x Rs 120) + 12.5% of Rs 60,000 = Rs 60,000 + Rs 7,500 = Rs 67,500.

q: A depot holds 600 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 20 per unit. Fresh receipts of 300 units at Rs 26 per unit and 100 units at Rs 32 per unit are taken into stock. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:

options.A: Rs 23 per unit
options.B: Rs 26 per unit
options.C: Rs 21 per unit
options.D: Rs 24 per unit

e: Revised book (average) rate = (600 x Rs 20 + 300 x Rs 26 + 100 x Rs 32) / 1,000 = Rs 23,000 / 1,000 = Rs 23 per unit.

q: An 'open tender' for stores purchase is one which is:

options.A: Advertised publicly, so that all eligible firms may submit their offers
options.B: Sent only to firms borne on the approved list for the item
options.C: Placed on a single firm without inviting offers
options.D: Opened without any fixed due date and time

e: An open tender under the Stores Code and GFR is advertised publicly through IREPS and newspapers so that all eligible firms can compete, unlike a limited tender restricted to approved firms or a single tender placed without competition.

q: Material is received in a depot and taken into priced stock, but the supplier's bill has not yet been passed for payment. In the general books, this receipt is initially accounted for by:

options.A: Debiting the Stock Adjustment Account
options.B: Debiting the priced stock account and crediting Purchase Suspense
options.C: Debiting the revenue head of the consuming department
options.D: Crediting the Sales Suspense Account

e: Receipts taken into priced stock before the supplier bill is paid are debited to stock and credited to Purchase Suspense; the suspense is cleared when the bill is passed and paid, keeping stock and payment linked.

q: A credit balance outstanding under 'Sales Suspense' represents:

options.A: Scrap which has been surveyed off but not yet auctioned
options.B: Stores issued to workshops for which no debit has been raised
options.C: Sale value deposited by purchasers, pending delivery of the material and adjustment to the final heads of account
options.D: Bills of suppliers received but not yet paid

e: Sales Suspense holds sale value deposited by purchasers pending delivery of scrap or stores; on completion of delivery the amount is transferred to the final revenue or stock heads, clearing the suspense.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Stock Adjustment Account:
1. A shortage of stock found in stock verification is debited to the Stock Adjustment Account.
2. An excess of stock found in stock verification is credited to the Stock Adjustment Account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under the Stores Code, shortages found on verification are debited and excesses credited to the Stock Adjustment Account pending investigation and approval, so both statements are correct.

q: For working out the Turnover Ratio of stores, the closing balance taken into account comprises:

options.A: Only the value of stores held in the main depot of the railway
options.B: Only the balances under Purchase Suspense
options.C: Only the value of scrap awaiting disposal
options.D: The value of priced stock in depots together with the balances under the stores suspense heads

e: Turnover Ratio is worked on total stores outlay against closing balance, which for this purpose means priced stock in depots plus balances under stores suspense heads such as Purchase and Sales Suspense, not stock in one depot alone.

q: Before the stores transactions of a month are posted in the general books, the Stores Monthly Summaries received from depots are agreed by the Stores Accounts office with:

options.A: The priced stores ledger summaries, so that the depot figures and the priced accounts agree
options.B: The tender notices issued during the month
options.C: The muster rolls of the depot staff
options.D: The auction catalogues of scrap lots

e: Stores Monthly Summaries from depots are agreed in the Stores Accounts office with the priced stores ledger summaries before posting to the general books, ensuring depot custody figures and priced accounts tally.

q: The stock sheet recording the difference between the physical balance and the book balance of an item is prepared by:

options.A: The supplier who supplied the item
options.B: The stock verifier who carried out the verification
options.C: The purchaser of scrap from the depot
options.D: The consuming department which draws the item

e: The stock sheet is prepared by the stock verifier or Inspector of Stores Accounts who verifies the item, recording book balance, physical balance and the difference for approval by the competent authority.

q: The narrative report submitted by the Inspector of Stores Accounts/Assistant Stock Verifier differs from a stock sheet in that the narrative report:

options.A: Records only the quantity difference of a single item
options.B: Is prepared by the stockholder himself
options.C: Is used for passing suppliers' bills for payment
options.D: Brings out procedural and system irregularities noticed during verification, for remedial action

e: A stock sheet records quantity difference for one item, while the narrative report brings out procedural and system irregularities, defective custody or accounting noticed during verification, for remedial action by the administration.

q: During stock verification a shortage of an item is recorded on a stock sheet. The shortage is adjusted in the accounts:

options.A: By the stock verifier himself, by altering the bin card
options.B: By recovering it in cash from the purchaser of scrap
options.C: After approval of the stock sheet by the competent authority, through the Stock Adjustment Account, with recovery from the stockholder where his responsibility is established
options.D: By debiting it to Purchase Suspense without any approval

e: A shortage on a stock sheet is adjusted only after approval by the competent authority through the Stock Adjustment Account; recovery is made from the stockholder where responsibility is established, otherwise it is written off under sanction.

q: Stores returned to a depot by a department and classified as 'repairable' are taken back into priced stock:

options.A: Only after they have been repaired and received back in the depot under a receipt note
options.B: Immediately on return, without any repair
options.C: Only after they are sold in an e-auction
options.D: Only at the close of the financial year

e: Repairable stores returned to depot are not taken into priced stock as serviceable on return; they are taken back only after repair and formal receipt under a receipt note, so that unrepaired material is not valued as usable stock.

q: Stores despatched by one depot to another depot on transfer are taken off the books of the despatching depot:

options.A: As soon as the material is loaded for despatch
options.B: Only when the receiving depot acknowledges receipt of the material
options.C: At the end of the financial year in which they are despatched
options.D: When the next stock verification of the despatching depot is held

e: On inter-depot transfer the despatching depot relieves its stock only after the receiving depot acknowledges receipt on the transfer note, preventing loss of accountal for material in transit between depots.

q: In the general books of a railway, the balance under the stores stock and suspense heads, taken together, broadly represents:

options.A: Only the earnest money held from tenderers
options.B: Only the value of stores sold to outside parties
options.C: Only the cost of stores consumed during the year
options.D: The value of stores in stock and in transit, together with the stores transactions awaiting final adjustment

e: Taken together, priced stock and stores suspense balances in the general books represent stores physically in stock and in transit plus transactions awaiting final adjustment, and not merely cash deposits or consumption.

q: The 'deduct entry' in the Stores Budget operates by way of:

options.A: A credit entry under Sales Suspense
options.B: An addition to the debits for stores required for workshops
options.C: A minus (deduct) entry against the stores debits, for the value of stores whose cost already stands provided in the estimates of works and programmes
options.D: A transfer of the closing stock balance to the Capital account

e: The deduct entry in the Stores Budget is a minus entry against stores debits for stores whose cost is already provided in works estimates and programmes, avoiding double provision of the same requirement in the budget.

q: Stores are issued from a depot for ordinary repairs and maintenance charged to revenue. The value of the issue is classified in the accounts of the consuming department under:

options.A: PU 27
options.B: PU 11
options.C: PU 32
options.D: PU 35

e: Stores issued for ordinary repairs and maintenance charged to revenue are classified under Primary Unit 27 - cost of material from stores, distinct from staff costs under PU 11 and other expenses under PU 32 or 35.

q: In a Stores Budget, 'credits' during the year arise when stores are:

options.A: Purchased from suppliers and received in depots
options.B: Issued to consuming departments and works, or sold
options.C: Ordered through purchase orders placed on firms
options.D: Verified physically by the stock verifiers

e: In the Stores Budget, debits arise on purchase and receipt of stores, while credits arise when stores are issued to departments and works or sold, reducing the stock and suspense balance.

q: Items which are both high in annual consumption value ('A' category) and vital in use are subjected to:

options.A: No special control, as they are stocked in every depot
options.B: Control only at the time of their disposal as scrap
options.C: The same loose control as low-value 'C' category items
options.D: The closest inventory control, with frequent review of stock levels and assured availability

e: Items that are both A category by annual consumption value and Vital by criticality need the closest control - frequent review, accurate forecasting and assured availability - because stock-out is costly and operationally critical.

q: ABC analysis and VED analysis of stores differ from each other in that:

options.A: ABC is based on criticality in use, while VED is based on annual consumption value
options.B: Both are based only on the unit price of the items
options.C: ABC classifies items by annual consumption value, while VED classifies them by their criticality in use
options.D: ABC is used for scrap items, while VED is used for stock items only

e: ABC analysis classifies items by annual consumption value into A, B and C, while VED analysis classifies by criticality in use as Vital, Essential and Desirable; the bases are value and criticality respectively.

q: FSN analysis is distinguished from SDE analysis of inventory in that:

options.A: FSN classifies items by their rate of movement from stock, while SDE classifies them by the ease or difficulty of obtaining them
options.B: FSN classifies items by their unit price, while SDE classifies them by annual consumption value
options.C: FSN is applied only to imported items, while SDE is applied only to indigenous items
options.D: Both analyses classify items by their criticality in use

e: FSN analysis classifies items as Fast, Slow and Non-moving by rate of movement from stock, while SDE classifies as Scarce, Difficult and Easy by ease or difficulty of procurement and availability.

q: An item has not been issued from a depot for more than 24 months, but it is firmly programmed for use in a planned overhaul falling within the next 24 months. The item is:

options.A: Dead surplus, to be surveyed off at once
options.B: Not dead surplus, as it is expected to be used within the next 24 months
options.C: Obsolete, as its design has changed
options.D: Scrap, as it has not moved for over two years

e: Dead surplus means stores not issued for over 24 months and not expected to be used in the next 24 months; an item firmly programmed for an overhaul within the next 24 months fails the second test and is not dead surplus.

q: Stores having a limited shelf life are issued from stock on the first-in-first-out basis mainly so that:

options.A: The newest stock is always consumed first
options.B: The book rate of the item keeps rising
options.C: The stock can be verified more easily
options.D: The oldest stock is consumed before its shelf life expires

e: Stores with limited shelf life are issued first-in-first-out so the oldest lot is consumed before expiry, preventing deterioration and loss; issuing newest first would leave old stock to expire.

q: Where pre-despatch inspection of stores is prescribed in a purchase order:

options.A: The consignee depot loses the right to inspect the material on receipt
options.B: Payment of the full bill must be made before despatch
options.C: The material is inspected before despatch, and the consignee still inspects it on receipt before acceptance into stock
options.D: No receipt note is required to be issued by the consignee depot

e: Pre-despatch inspection under the purchase order does not displace consignee inspection; material is inspected before despatch and again checked and inspected on receipt by the consignee before acceptance into stock.

q: Stores supplied under a contract are found defective within the warranty period and the supplier replaces them. For the replacement stores:

options.A: No fresh payment is made, the replacement being supplied free of cost under the warranty clause
options.B: A fresh purchase order at current market rates must be placed
options.C: Payment is made at double the original rate as compensation
options.D: The depot pays only the inspection charges to the supplier

e: Defective stores replaced within warranty are supplied free of cost under the warranty clause in the GCC for Supply and the contract; no fresh purchase order or fresh payment is made for the replacement.

q: A supplier offers stores which do not fully conform to the specification but are usable for the intended purpose. Such stores may be accepted:

options.A: By the depot storekeeper at the full contract price
options.B: By the competent authority under a deviation, with a suitable reduction in price
options.C: Only after they are first sold in an e-auction
options.D: In no circumstances, even by the competent authority

e: Stores deviating from specification but usable for the intended purpose may be accepted only by the competent authority under a deviation sanction with a suitable price reduction; a storekeeper cannot accept them at full price.

q: In a Stores Tender Committee, the specific responsibility of the Finance/Accounts member is to ensure that:

options.A: The material is inspected at the supplier's premises
options.B: The stock in the depot is physically verified
options.C: The scrap lots are correctly prepared for auction
options.D: Funds are available, financial propriety is observed and the rates recommended for acceptance are reasonable

e: The Finance member of a Tender Committee ensures availability of funds, financial propriety, reasonableness of rates and compliance with procurement rules before recommending acceptance, as required for stores tenders.

q:
Consider the following statements about vetting of indents by Finance:
1. Vetting examines the availability of funds and the propriety of the demand.
2. Vetting of an indent for a stock item examines its justification with reference to the item's AAC and the coverage already available.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Finance vetting of indents examines fund availability and propriety of demand, and for stock items also justification against Annual Average Consumption and existing coverage, so both statements are correct.

q: An officer proposes to buy stores by single tender, otherwise than against a Proprietary Article Certificate, merely because an open tender would take more time. The proposal can be accepted only:

options.A: With recorded justification and the sanction of the competent authority with finance concurrence
options.B: On the verbal orders of the depot officer
options.C: If the storekeeper certifies that the rates are reasonable
options.D: If the item is required before the end of the financial year

e: Single tender otherwise than on a Proprietary Article Certificate is an exception to open competition under GFR and the Stores Code; it needs recorded justification, sanction of the competent authority and finance concurrence, not merely speed.

q: Stores covered by a Proprietary Article Certificate are procured from:

options.A: The lowest bidder in an open tender
options.B: The proprietary firm (original equipment manufacturer) or its authorised dealer/agent
options.C: Any registered firm dealing in similar items
options.D: The Government e-Marketplace, in all cases

e: Items covered by a Proprietary Article Certificate are procured only from the proprietary firm, the original equipment manufacturer, or its authorised dealer or agent, since no other source can supply the proprietary item.

q: Reverse auction for purchase of stores is distinguished from e-auction for sale of scrap in that:

options.A: In both, the bids move upwards from the starting price
options.B: In both, the bids move downwards from the starting price
options.C: Reverse auction is conducted offline, while e-auction is conducted on IREPS
options.D: In reverse auction bidders quote successively lower prices to obtain the order, while in e-auction bidders quote successively higher prices to buy the scrap

e: In reverse auction for purchase, bidders successively lower prices to win the order, while in e-auction for scrap disposal bidders successively raise prices to buy the lot; the direction of bidding is opposite.

q: In the two-packet system, the price packet of a bidder whose techno-commercial offer is found unacceptable is:

options.A: Opened along with the other price packets
options.B: Opened first, before the techno-commercial packet
options.C: Not opened, the price bids of only the technically acceptable bidders being opened
options.D: Sent to the Finance member for a separate decision

e: In the two-packet system only techno-commercially acceptable bidders proceed; the price packet of an unacceptable bidder is not opened, preserving fairness and preventing price influencing the technical decision.

q: A consuming department urgently requires an item which is covered by an existing rate contract. The requirement is met by:

options.A: Placing a supply order on the rate-contract firm, as and when required, at the contracted rate
options.B: Inviting a fresh open tender for the quantity required
options.C: Declaring the item as dead surplus
options.D: Purchasing the item through an e-auction

e: Where a rate contract is in force, the consuming department meets its need by placing supply orders on the rate contract firm as required at the contracted rate, without inviting a fresh tender for each requirement.

q: A rate (running) contract differs from a definite quantity contract in respect of quantity in that a rate contract:

options.A: Commits the Railway to purchase one fixed total quantity in a single lot
options.B: Does not commit the Railway to a total quantity; supplies are ordered as and when required at the fixed rate
options.C: Is used only for quantities fixed by the Railway Board
options.D: Requires the entire quantity to be supplied on the first day of the contract

e: A rate or running contract fixes rate, terms and period but does not commit the Railway to a total quantity; supplies are ordered as and when required, unlike a definite quantity contract for a fixed total quantity.

q: A risk purchase is made against a defaulting supplier at a price higher than the original contract price. The amount recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:

options.A: The full price paid for the risk purchase
options.B: Only the earnest money deposited by him
options.C: Nothing, as the Railway bears the extra cost itself
options.D: The excess of the risk purchase cost over the price payable under the original contract, together with other losses recoverable under the contract

e: On risk purchase, the defaulting supplier is liable under the GCC for Supply for the excess of risk purchase cost over the original contract price plus other recoverable losses, not the entire risk purchase price.

q: A supplier delays the supply of stores beyond the delivery period and liquidated damages become leviable. The liquidated damages are ordinarily recovered from:

options.A: The pay of the depot storekeeper
options.B: The sale proceeds of the next scrap auction
options.C: The supplier's bills or his security deposit held by the Railway
options.D: The earnest money of the other tenderers in the tender

e: Liquidated damages for delayed supply are recovered from the supplier dues under the contract - his pending bills or security deposit - as provided in the liquidated damages clause, and not from unrelated persons.

q: A firm exempted from payment of Earnest Money Deposit in a stores tender is, on acceptance of its tender:

options.A: Still required to furnish the prescribed Security Deposit for due fulfilment of the contract
options.B: Also exempted from furnishing any Security Deposit
options.C: Required to furnish double the prescribed Security Deposit
options.D: Required to pay the earnest money with interest

e: Exemption from Earnest Money Deposit, for example for registered MSEs or approved firms, does not exempt the successful tenderer from furnishing the prescribed Security Deposit for due fulfilment of the contract.

q: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, where the lowest bid is of a non-local supplier, a Class-I local supplier whose bid is within the margin of purchase preference is:

options.A: Debarred from the tender for not being the lowest
options.B: Given an opportunity to match the lowest price and, on so matching, considered for award of the order
options.C: Awarded the order at its own quoted price without matching
options.D: Required to furnish additional earnest money before award

e: Under the Make in India Order, a Class-I local supplier within the purchase preference margin over a non-local L1 is given a chance to match the L1 price and, on matching, is considered for award.

q: A micro/small enterprise has quoted a price within the price band of L1 + 15% in a stores tender. Under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs, the enterprise may be allowed to:

options.A: Supply the entire order at its own quoted price
options.B: Claim exemption from inspection of its supplies
options.C: Reject the tender conditions and supply on its own terms
options.D: Supply up to 25% of the total order quantity by matching the L1 price

e: Under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs Order 2012, an MSE quoting within L1 plus 15 percent may supply up to 25 percent of the order quantity by matching the L1 price.

q: The 'book examination clause' in a stores contract is exercised by:

options.A: The depot storekeeper, by examining the bin cards of the depot
options.B: The purchaser of scrap, by examining the auction catalogue
options.C: An authorised representative of the Railway, by examining the contractor's books of account and cost records to verify the costs and prices claimed
options.D: The supplier, by examining the Railway's priced stores ledger

e: The book examination clause entitles an authorised Railway representative to examine the contractor books, accounts and cost records to verify costs and prices claimed under the contract.

q: During the currency of a stores contract, the contractor sells the same item to another buyer at a rate lower than the railway contract rate. Under the fall clause:

options.A: The contract stands automatically cancelled
options.B: The lower rate applies to the supplies made to the Railway also
options.C: The Railway must pay the difference to the contractor
options.D: The contractor is debarred from all future tenders at once

e: Under the fall clause, if the contractor sells the same item to another buyer at a lower rate during the contract currency, that lower rate applies to supplies to the Railway as well.

q: Midway through a stores contract, the Railway needs an additional quantity of the same item urgently. By invoking the option clause in the contract, the Railway may:

options.A: Place the additional quantity with a different firm at any rate
options.B: Order the additional quantity from the same contractor on the same rates, terms and conditions during the currency of the contract
options.C: Cancel the original contract and invite fresh tenders
options.D: Direct the contractor to supply the quantity free of cost

e: The option clause allows the Railway, during the currency of the contract, to order an additional quantity from the same contractor on the same rates and terms, without a fresh tender for that additional quantity.

q: A supplier demands a higher price during the currency of a contract on the ground that market prices have risen. Under the price variation clause, any adjustment of price is worked out:

options.A: At the rate demanded by the supplier
options.B: At the discretion of the consignee depot
options.C: Only after approval of the Railway Board in each case
options.D: With reference to the indices and the formula stipulated in the contract itself

e: A price variation claim is admissible only as worked out by the indices and formula stipulated in the price variation clause of the contract itself; the supplier demand or depot discretion does not govern it.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence for disposal of unserviceable stores as scrap?

options.A: E-auction, survey/condemnation, delivery to the purchaser
options.B: Delivery to the purchaser, survey/condemnation, e-auction
options.C: Survey/condemnation by the Survey Committee and sanction, sale by e-auction, delivery to the purchaser on payment of the sale value
options.D: Survey/condemnation, delivery to the purchaser, payment of the sale value thereafter

e: Unserviceable stores are disposed of in sequence - survey and condemnation by the Survey Committee with sanction, sale by e-auction, and delivery to the purchaser only after payment of the full sale value.

q: The reserve price fixed for a lot of scrap offered in an e-auction is:

options.A: Not disclosed to the bidders in the auction catalogue
options.B: Printed in the auction catalogue for the information of bidders
options.C: Fixed by the highest bidder at the start of the auction
options.D: The same as the earnest money for the lot

e: The reserve or upset price for a scrap lot is fixed by the competent authority but is not disclosed in the auction catalogue; disclosure would anchor bidding and defeat realisation of the best price.

q: The auction catalogue published before an e-auction of scrap serves the bidders by giving:

options.A: The names of the bidders who will participate in the auction
options.B: Lot-wise description of the scrap, its location and the conditions of sale, so that bidders can inspect the lots and bid
options.C: The price at which each lot will finally be sold
options.D: The book rates of all stock items held in the depot

e: The auction catalogue gives lot-wise description, location and conditions of sale so intending bidders can inspect lots before bidding; it does not disclose final sale prices or bidder names.

q: After the full sale value of a scrap lot has been paid and a delivery order issued, the purchaser is required to:

options.A: Wait for the Railway to deliver the material at his premises free of cost
options.B: Take a fresh purchase order from the depot
options.C: Pay the sale value again at the time of delivery
options.D: Load and remove the material from the depot at his own cost within the stipulated delivery period

e: After payment of full sale value and issue of a delivery order, the purchaser must load and remove the material at his own cost within the stipulated delivery period, failing which ground rent or forfeiture may apply.

q: Before the value of stores issued from a depot is posted to the account of a consuming department or work, the Stores Accounts office checks, on the priced issue note, the:

options.A: Name of the supplier who originally supplied the item
options.B: Date on which the item was last verified by the stock verifier
options.C: Head of account (allocation) to which the issue is to be debited
options.D: Earnest money deposited by the tenderer for the item

e: Before posting an issue, Stores Accounts checks the allocation - the head of account shown on the priced issue note - so the value is debited to the correct department, work or revenue head.

q: Stores bills have been paid and a debit is outstanding under Purchase Suspense. The material, when received, is rejected on inspection and returned to the supplier. The outstanding debit is cleared when:

options.A: The depot writes off the amount on its own authority
options.B: The replacement material is received and accepted, or the amount is otherwise recovered from the supplier and linked with the payment
options.C: The next stock verification of the depot is completed
options.D: The material is offered for sale as scrap

e: A Purchase Suspense debit for paid but rejected material is cleared when replacement is received and accepted or the amount is recovered from the supplier and linked to the original payment; it is not written off by the depot.

q: During stock verification of a depot, a shortage of one stores item and an excess of a similar, but distinct, stores item are found. The correct treatment is that:

options.A: The shortage and the excess are netted off against each other and no stock sheet is prepared
options.B: Only the shortage is recorded, as the excess belongs to the depot
options.C: Separate stock sheets are prepared for the shortage and for the excess, and each difference is adjusted on its own merits after approval
options.D: Both differences are ignored if their values are nearly equal

e: Shortage and excess of distinct items, even if similar, are not netted off; separate stock sheets are prepared for each item and each difference is investigated and adjusted on its own merits after approval.

q: An item is of low annual consumption value ('C' category in ABC analysis) but is classified as 'Vital' in VED analysis, its non-availability being capable of stopping train operations. The item is controlled so that:

options.A: No stock is held, as 'C' category items need no control
options.B: Stock is reviewed only once in a few years
options.C: It is ordered only after a complete stock-out occurs
options.D: Despite its low value, assured availability is maintained through adequate safety stock and watch on its stock position

e: A C category item that is Vital needs assured availability despite low value; adequate safety stock and close watch on stock position are kept because its stock-out can stop train operations.

q: Scrap of small value is sold by a depot for cash to a purchaser. Until the sale is finally adjusted in the accounts, the cash received is required to be:

options.A: Remitted promptly to the Railway Cash Office for credit under Sales Suspense, and not retained or spent by the depot
options.B: Retained by the storekeeper for meeting petty depot expenses
options.C: Deposited in the personal account of the depot officer
options.D: Adjusted directly against the cost of new stores purchased

e: Cash received for small-value scrap sales must be promptly remitted to the Railway Cash Office for credit to Sales Suspense pending final adjustment; the depot cannot retain or spend it.

q: Material supplied against a purchase order is rejected on inspection as defective. Before the rejection becomes final, the supplier seeks an opportunity to make good the defects. The correct course is that:

options.A: The material must in all cases be returned at once, rectification being never permissible
options.B: The depot storekeeper may accept the material after informal repair at the depot
options.C: The supplier may be allowed to rectify, repair or replace the defective material within the period and in the manner advised in the rejection communication, after which the material is re-inspected
options.D: The material is sold to the supplier himself in an e-auction

e: Rejection is not always immediate return; the supplier may be allowed, within the period and manner advised in the rejection memo, to rectify, repair or replace the defect, after which the material is re-inspected before acceptance.
